title: SLO variance stabilization and dashboard primer
author: Priya Shah
content:
Overview

This primer describes a repeatable approach for identifying, stabilizing, and visualizing SLO variance across the LLM inference platform. It covers: how variance arises, investigative workflows, dashboard patterns for rapid operator triage, and a lightweight stabilization playbook for short-to-medium term remediation. The goal is to reduce noisy SLO flips, shorten oncall burn, and produce clear operator signals for capacity and quality workstreams.

Key definitions

- SLI: observed measurement (latency, availability, correctness).
- SLO: target for an SLI (example: 99th percentile latency <= 250ms).
- Variance: sustained or transient movement in an SLI distribution that increases SLO burn without actionable root cause.
- Noise: high-frequency small changes that falsely trigger alerts.

Why SLO variance matters for LLM inference

- Tokenized workloads produce heavy outliers (longer sequences, multi-turn chat) which inflate tail latencies.
- Auto-scaling and burst routing introduce non-stationary capacity.
- Model swaps/rollouts change compute characteristics; small changes in prompt distributions can change token counts and decoding costs.
- Instrumentation sampling and aggregation windows can mask bursts or amplify noise.

Detecting variance early: signals to watch

1) Burst patterns in SLO burn curve that do not line up with other system-level metrics (GPU utilization, queue depth).
2) Discrepancies between tokenized cost metrics and raw request counts.
3) Cross-region divergence: same tenant has different SLI behavior in another region.
4) Increased correlation of tail latency with specific model variants or with prefix-cache misses.

Dashboard patterns (recommended panels)

Top-level dashboard (single-screen for paging):
- SLO burn timeline (1h/6h/24h windows) with annotation band for rolling deploys.
- Token-rate vs request-rate heatmap to reveal shifting token distribution.
- 99th/95th/50th latency series per model-variant (stacked small multiples).
- Prefetch/KV-cache hit ratio and average KV lookup time.
- Queue depth and per-tenant priority-slice occupancy.
- Operator action timeline (manual evictions, model swaps, scale events).

Investigation view (linked from top-level):
- Sampled request trace table (columns: timestamp, tenant, model, seq_len, prefix_hit, decoding_ms, serving_node).
- Cold-start/warm-start marker overlay.
- Correlation matrix: SLO burn vs GPU throttling, host OOMs, network errors.
- Histogram: sequence length distribution comparing current window vs baseline.

Operator-friendly widgets (search/filterable):
- Quick filter for affected tenants.
- Toggle to switch between token-normalized and request-normalized views.
- Runbook link and one-click PagerDuty escalation button.

Recommended telemetry and query examples

Metrics to collect (minimally):
- request.count (tags: tenant, model_variant, region, priority)
- request.tokens.total and request.tokens.prompt/completion
- serve.latency.decode_ms (percentiles + exemplar traces)
- kv_cache.hit and kv_cache.miss (per-tenant)
- queue.depth and queue.wait_ms
- gpu.utilization and gpu.sched_delay_ms
- deploy.rollout_id and operator.eviction_event (annotation metrics)

PromQL examples (Grafana/Prometheus):
- 99th latency per model:
  quantile_over_time(0.99, serve_latency_decode_ms_bucket{job=\"runtime\", model_variant=~\".*\"}[1h])
- Token-normalized 99th:
  (quantile_over_time(0.99, serve_latency_decode_ms_bucket[1h]) / avg_over_time(request_tokens_total[1h])) * 1000
- SLO burn (5m sliding):
  sum(rate(serve_latency_slo_violation[5m])) / sum(rate(request_count[5m]))

Alert design guidance

- Use multi-signal rules: require both SLO burn rate > threshold AND one secondary signal (queue depth > X OR token-rate spike > Y) to reduce noise.
- Use graded notifications: page on sustained burn (>= 15m) or large single-interval burn spike (> 3x baseline).
- Suppress alerts during scheduled rollouts using rollout_id annotation windows.
- Provide actionable alert text with immediate triage steps and links to the investigation view.

Stabilization playbook (15–90 day cadence)

Short-term (minutes–hours):
1) Throttle noisy tenants using soft-priority reduce (operator tool).
2) Route affected requests to a compatible lower-cost model variant (fallback policy) to buy time.
3) Increase sampling rate for traces for the affected window.
4) Open a P0 incident if burn persists beyond 30 minutes with growing SLO debt.

Medium-term (days–weeks):
1) Reconcile token accounting: ensure token-normalized SLO panels are visible to product and platform.
2) Adjust autoscaler warmup parameters to reduce oscillation (min replicas, startup_probe tuning).
3) Run A/B on compiler/kernel switch if runtime patching is suspected.
4) Add targeted prefetch cohorts for high-variance tenants.

Long-term (weeks–quarters):
1) Model onboarding checklist: require per-sequence-length perf profile and SLO impact test.
2) Kernel and quantization profiles gated by SLO sensitivity matrix.
3) Tenant-level budgeting and higher-fidelity throttles tied to billing signals.

Runbook: immediate triage steps (operator-facing)

1) Confirm: check SLO burn dashboard and cross-check region and model-variant panels.
2) Fetch exemplar traces for top 10 violating requests (use trace-explorer or trace_id list).
3) Check for recent deploys (deploy.rollout_id) and operator actions.
4) If token spike: switch dashboard to token-normalized view; share findings on incident channel.
5) If queueing: check per-node eviction logs and reassign tenant to alternate pool if available.
6) Apply soft-priority throttle for the tenant for 5–30 minutes and observe burn response.
7) If mitigated, file a stabilization ticket with owners (platform infra + tenant product team).

Post-incident retrospective template (to be filed after stabilization)

- Incident summary (1 paragraph).
- Timeline (5m resolution for first 60 minutes, 15m thereafter).
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence.
- Short-term mitigations applied and effectiveness.
- Medium/long-term actions and owners with due dates.
- Learnings for model onboarding and SLO definitions.

Dashboard maintenance and ownership

- Dashboard steward: platform-observability (primary) and runtime-team (secondary).
- Monthly checklist:
  - Validate exemplar traces sampling rate.
  - Verify alert thresholds against rolling 90-day baseline.
  - Confirm annotation pipeline is capturing deploys and operator events.
  - Run synthetic scenarios (prefetch miss, token spike) quarterly.

Example configuration table (dashboard panels & owner):

| panel_id | title | refresh | primary_owner | query_hint |
| P1 | SLO burn (1h/6h/24h) | 15s | platform-observability | slo_burn_rate() with rollout annotations |
| P2 | Token-rate vs request-rate heatmap | 30s | runtime-team | rate(request_tokens_total[1m]) / rate(request_count[1m]) |
| P3 | 99/95/50 latencies by model-variant | 15s | runtime-team | quantile_over_time(...) |
| P4 | KV-cache hit ratio by tenant | 30s | cache-service | sum(kv_cache_hit) / sum(kv_cache_hit + kv_cache_miss) |
| P5 | Queue depth and eviction events | 15s | platform-allocator | rate(queue_depth[1m]) and operator.eviction_event |

(Panel table above should be copied into the dashboard metadata when creating the Grafana dashboard.)

Acceptance criteria for stabilization work items

- Reduce false pages by >= 60% for the affected alert channel over a 30-day window.
- Maintain SLO compliance within 1.5x of baseline tail for 90 days post-change.
- Ensure token-normalized and request-normalized SLO views are reconciled in the next oncall rotation.

Appendix: useful CLI and queries

- Fetch top traces (pseudo-CLI):
  rtxctl traces query --start=now-1h --end=now --filter=\"slo_violation:true\" --group-by=model_variant --limit=50

- Soft-priority throttle example (operator API):
  curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN\" https://api.internal.redwood/v1/tenants/THX-123/actions \\
    -d '{"action":"set_priority", "priority":"soft_reduced", "duration_minutes":30 }'

- Example alert text (template):
  [PAGING] SLO burn exceeded for runtime service in region {{region}}
  Symptoms: 99th latency spike, queue depth rising, token-rate above baseline
  Immediate actions: 1) Check traces dashboard 2) Apply soft-priority throttle 3) Verify recent rollouts
  Links: {{dashboard_url}} | {{runbook_link}}

Notes and known caveats

- Token-normalized views require correct instrumentation upstream; partial coverage will produce misleading normalization.
- Some model variants have non-linear decoding characteristics (e.g., sampling-based decoding) which appear as high variance—treat these specially in onboarding.
- Avoid aggressive autoscaler reaction to short token bursts; prefer smoothing windows aligned to SLO windows.

Contacts and escalation path

- Primary: platform-observability (pager: #platform-oncall)
- Secondary: runtime-team (pager: #runtime-oncall)
- Escalation: SRE manager on-call if incident remains P0 after 60 minutes.

Related artifacts

- Model onboarding performance checklist (link to models page).
- KV-cache consistency playbook.
- Token-cost attribution spec.

This document should be used as the baseline for any new dashboard or alert related to SLO variance. If you make changes to panels or thresholds, add an entry to the dashboard changelog and notify the platform-observability mailing list.
